titleEn: Death through the lens of evolution: why didn't nature design us to live forever?
summaryEn:
People often see death as a tragedy, a failure of the body or a fault that needs fixing. But from the perspective of evolutionary biology, death is not exactly a mistake.

Evolution is not aimed at producing immortal individuals. Its only "goal" is to help genes pass to the next generation. So what matters most to evolution is not how long you live, but whether you leave a next generation behind.
